retries_detail: SecurityAutoConfigurationTest's chain assertion failed three times before it was right: no HandlerMappingIntrospector (needed WebMvcAutoConfiguration on the runner), then the ordering assertion failed and revealed the defect it was written to look for, then the assertion that the resolver is in effect had to be rewritten from inspecting a bean - the resolver is not one - to running the chain's bearer filter against an lpat_ credential.

RevocationWindowValidationTest's two-term-constructor fixture was wrong on the first attempt: 1m+1m+4m breached a 5m ceiling on the request/response path, so it failed for a reason unrelated to what it was asserting. Re-cut with a three-second margin so any non-zero default for the new term would breach it.

PatDirectAuthenticationIT failed to load its context twice: a type mismatch (PatService.IssuedToken, not PatTokens.MintedToken, and PatSnapshot carries no key id so the lookup goes through IssuedToken.token().id()), then an ambiguous mapping because the protected endpoint was both component-scanned and declared as a @Bean.

defects_found_by_this_change: The PAT filter was unreachable. Task 4.4 specified 'register it before the bearer filter', copying the mTLS filter's justification. Spring Security orders BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter ahead of BasicAuthenticationFilter - the position this module adds every filter at, stripping included - so the filter was registered after it; and BearerTokenAuthenticationFilter authenticates unconditionally and on failure commences the entry point without continuing the chain, so it answered 401 on the lpat_ credential whatever ran before it. Moving the filter would not have fixed it. Fixed with PatAwareBearerTokenResolver, installed only when the filter is enabled. Found because the task demanded the assertion be made against SecurityFilterChain.getFilters() rather than against the configuration; a configuration-reading test would have passed throughout. SecurityAutoConfigurationTest.defaultResolverIsUntouchedWithoutTheFilter now asserts the 401 still happens without the resolver, so the defect is pinned rather than only repaired.

The introspection endpoint was unreachable by its only caller. It sits behind the chain's anyRequest().authenticated() while PatIntrospectionClient carries no credential of its own - the only credential in the exchange is the token being asked about, which is the subject of the question rather than the caller's identity. Every introspection received a 401 and failed closed, refusing every token. Invisible from either half: PatIntrospectionIT authenticates a SERVICE principal before calling the endpoint, and the filter's unit test mocks the client. Found by PatDirectAuthenticationIT driving the whole loop over real HTTP. Fixed by extending PatExchangeConfigurationValidator's existing public-path warning to cover the mounted introspection path, on the same warn-not-fail reasoning it already applies to /oauth2/token.
scope_changes: Task 4.4 was rewritten and task 4.4a added, because the task as written was wrong rather than merely incomplete. The spec requirement, the filter javadoc and the chain comment all record the mistaken reasoning rather than quietly replacing it: 'before the bearer filter, because a PAT request carries no bearer JWT' reads as obviously correct, which is exactly why it needs a note.
Task 5.3 added for the introspection reachability fix, which no task anticipated.

Whether PatIntrospectionClient should be able to present a credential of its own, for a deployment wanting application-level caller authentication on introspection rather than relying on the mesh. RFC 7662 asks for it. Not done here: it needs a service-identity mechanism the module nearest the bottom of the reactor does not have, and adding token acquisition there would be paid for by every platform consumer. Recorded as an open question; worth revisiting with the MCP starter, which faces the same question for its own outbound calls.

unmechanisable_conventions.note: Taken from six to eight by this change and recorded in both locales of build/architecture-rules/README.md, deliberately not trimmed to make the group look complete. The newest additions are that no check can assert a deployment actually removed the scaffolding when its edge gains PAT support, and that no check can verify the introspection endpoint is in fact reachable only inside the mesh. The public-path requirement itself IS mechanised, as a startup warning in PatExchangeConfigurationValidator, matching the precedent the exchange path already set - a warning rather than a build failure because the module cannot see whether an application published the path through its own SecurityFilterChain.
